title: Contracts and Control-Flow Analysis
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of contracts and control-flow analysis using at least one correct term from the lesson.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Contracts and Control-Flow Analysis** as part of **Advanced Kotlin Language Features**. Flow represents an asynchronous stream collected from a coroutine; flow operators, cancellation, buffering, and sharing determine behavior. Use the subtopics—Contract Concepts, Effects on Compiler Analysis, Version and Stability Considerations—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.run_instructions: This example requires kotlinx-coroutines-core (and the matching Flow APIs where used). Run it in a Kotlin/JVM Gradle project; do not paste it into a plain browser preview.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A suspend function always runs on a background thread automatically.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
